clue.text: War that's contrived wrongly?

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially arranged, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the word that, with its 's acting only as a link

explanation.surface: A war that was engineered on false pretences was a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges WAR plus THAT; the question mark admits the definition is a slightly unusual sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The old adverb also means perversely or awry, as well as across, so things going wrongly have gone that way.

clue.text: Applaud current demand

parts.note: AC is alternating current
to demand something is to claim it

explanation.surface: Cheer on the latest demand from protesters.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud is to praise loudly and publicly, a near synonym.

clue.text: Suspended sentence

definitions.meaning: dangling or held up from above
the death penalty carried out on the gallows

explanation.surface: A suspended sentence handed down in court.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'suspended sentence' looks like the legal term for a deferred penalty, but each word is a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dangling is suspended, and a gallows death sentence is called by the same word.

clue.text: Inappropriate article about rest

indicators.note: the article goes round the word for rest, enclosing it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
to lie down is to rest

explanation.surface: A grammar note calls an article placed near the word rest unsuitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foreign to a setting is out of place, unsuitable to it.

clue.text: One for the road-or maybe not!

definitions.text: One for the road-or maybe not!

parts.words: One for the road-or maybe not!
parts.note: one for the road usually means a last drink before leaving; read literally it is a person who takes to the road, though perhaps a stay-at-home will not be one

explanation.surface: A barman offers a last drink before the journey, then thinks better of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A journeyer is literally someone whose business is on the road.

clue.text: Edward harbours ill-feeling if beaten

indicators.note: to harbour is to hold within, so the name contains the resentment

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward
having the hump is British slang for sulky resentment

explanation.surface: Edward bears a grudge about being defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The hump' is British slang for a bad mood or resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten can mean struck repeatedly, which is exactly what heavy blows do.

clue.text: Drink the health of a high-minded individual?

definitions.meaning: raise a glass in honour of someone
a person celebrated by everyone, held high in the minds of the town

explanation.surface: Raise a glass to a principled person.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on 'the toast of the town', a person everyone holds in high regard; 'high-minded' usually means principled.
explanation.definitionFit: To drink someone's health is to propose a salute in their honour, and the celebrated person is the town's favourite.

clue.text: Anne ruled badly, being inadequately trained

indicators.note: done badly, so the letters of the two words come out scrambled

explanation.surface: Queen Anne governed poorly because she had no proper education.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without schooling or instruction is ignorant, poorly educated.

clue.text: Detectives getting into a hole colour

indicators.note: the detectives go inside the hole

parts.note: a pit is a hole in the ground
G-men are FBI agents in American slang

explanation.surface: Police officers climb down into a pit and find something colourful.
explanation.definitionFit: A colouring substance such as paint pigment gives things their hue.

clue.text: See this as an episcopal charge

definitions.text: See this as an episcopal charge

parts.words: See this as an episcopal charge
parts.note: a bishop's see is the area entrusted to his care, so the clue asks for that district

explanation.surface: A suggestion to view something as a duty belonging to a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like the verb to look, but it is the noun for a bishop's seat and territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's district is his see, the territory placed in his care.

clue.text: Shavian heroine, quite plain, with a following

indicators.note: the letter comes after the first piece

parts.note: candid means frank and plain-spoken

explanation.surface: A character from George Bernard Shaw is very straightforward and has fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Shavian means of George Bernard Shaw; his play is named for its heroine. 'with a following' looks like having fans but puts A after.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's 1894 play is named after its central woman, the vicar's wife.

clue.text: Brisk and adaptable gaoler about 50

indicators.note: the rearranged word goes around the number
something adaptable can be changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A lively, flexible jailer of about fifty years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adaptable' rearranges GAOLER (British spelling of jailer) and 'about' places L, Roman fifty, within it.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the tempo marking means lively and fast.

clue.text: Getting dressed

parts.note: in drill, troops dress when they line up straight, not when they put clothes on

explanation.surface: Putting on clothes in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: Military 'dressing' is lining up in a straight row.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing ranks means arranging soldiers into a straight line.

clue.text: Sharp ridge offering some rare television pictures

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used

explanation.surface: Rarely seen TV footage of a mountain crest.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountaineering term for a narrow knife-edged crest between glaciated valleys.

clue.text: The wise man affects a smug look

indicators.note: to affect is to put on or alter, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: The sage puts on a self-satisfied expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affects' rearranges A SMUG; 'look' is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The singular of magi, as in the three wise men of the nativity.

clue.text: The way to publicise package flight

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
to air something is to make it public
a case is a box or container

explanation.surface: Advice on marketing a holiday deal with air travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like air travel, tying in with 'package', but it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps is a set of them between floors.

clue.text: This is held up to the viewers as helpful

definitions.text: This is held up to the viewers as helpful

parts.words: This is held up to the viewers as helpful
parts.note: viewers here are the eyes, and the object is lifted up to them on a handle to aid sight

explanation.surface: Something is presented to the audience as useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewers' suggests an audience but means eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: These eyeglasses are held up on a long handle to aid vision.

clue.text: Twisted and turned when quite unnecessary

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Writhing and turning when it was totally pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surplus to requirements is superfluous, no longer needed.

clue.text: Wanted to imbibe pop, lost all hope of it

indicators.note: to imbibe is to take in, so the first word takes in the second

parts.note: desired means wanted
pa and pop both mean father

explanation.surface: Someone longed to drink fizzy pop but gave up hope of getting any.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' suggests a fizzy drink, matching 'imbibe', but it means father. 'of it' completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing every expectation of success is to give way to hopelessness.

clue.text: Underworld girl's fire

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and his realm
a miss is a girl or young woman; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A gangster's girlfriend's passion.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone is to sack them from a job.

clue.text: Nought's wrong where coercion is involved

indicators.note: letters arranged wrongly come out in a different order

parts.note: the plural noughts, zeros, read with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Zero is incorrect when force is used.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the adjective in 'shotgun wedding', a marriage forced on the couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A forced marriage is called a shotgun wedding, implying compulsion by threat.

clue.text: Backing a fiddle to appear game

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the instrument's name is read backwards

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin

explanation.surface: Supporting a swindle looks like a sporting move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' suggests a swindle but is a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub sport of throwing small missiles at a board is one example of a game.

clue.text: Note animosity, but stay

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
spite is malicious ill will

explanation.surface: Register the hostility, but remain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stay' looks like a verb but is the noun, as in a stay of execution.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay of execution is a temporary reprieve or break.

clue.text: Trickery of the French in a sense

indicators.note: the French article goes inside the word for a sense

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses
le is French for the

explanation.surface: The French have a kind of cunning sensibility.
explanation.walkthrough: As in sleight of hand, a conjuror's deft trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is a deceptive dexterity, so the word means cunning deception.

clue.text: Sunday drive to see the river

parts.note: a drive is a trip or excursion

explanation.surface: A weekend car trip to visit the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stour is a name shared by several English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Several English waterways bear this name, such as the one in Constable country.

clue.text: Stole a gun to exchange for food

indicators.note: letters exchanged swap places, giving a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A thief took a gun to swap for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny lobster or crawfish is a seafood delicacy.

clue.text: Vassal spreading a misleading story about for instance

indicators.note: the story goes around the abbreviation, holding it within

parts.note: a lie is an untrue tale
eg is short for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A feudal tenant spreads a false tale about an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' joins the surface: the lie is spread round the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal terms the word can mean a loyal subject owing service to a lord.

clue.text: Grouping in the herbaceous borders

indicators.note: the word is found inside the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: An arrangement of plants in the flowerbeds of a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: In biology this is a taxonomic rank between class and family.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxonomic rank, as in biology, is a category or classification.

clue.text: Stylish file one really doesn't appreciate

parts.note: in means fashionable
to grate is to rasp or file down

explanation.surface: A fancy nail file is something a person truly dislikes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ungrateful person fails to value kindness shown to them.

clue.text: Reckon on a swimmer getting muddled

parts.note: to add is to count or reckon up
the ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Counting a fish leaves one confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' is a crossword favourite for a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To addle is to confuse, so the participle means becoming confused.

clue.text: Honest as engineers

parts.note: since and as both mean because
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers are straightforward people.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine and truthful are both near synonyms.

clue.text: The distress of people in the wrong situation

indicators.note: the people are placed inside the word for a wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men means people

explanation.surface: The anguish of folk caught in a bad place.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony or acute suffering, mental or physical.
